newsitem.title: USA: Full House revenues rise on joint ventures.
newsitem.headline: Full House revenues rise on joint ventures.

text.p: Full House Resorts Inc said Monday it attributed its increase in net operating revenues for its fiscal year to additional revenues from its joint venture projects with Dreamport Inc.
Earlier, Full House reported a 1996 net loss of $760,600 on revenues of $7.67 million versus a loss of $5.55 million on $5.63 million in revenues.

Joint venture income increased in 1996 as a result of the inclusion of the fees from The Mill Casino for a full year, reimbursement of prior years' expenses by Dreamport and management fees received by one of the joint venture companies from the Midway Slots and Simulcast project which opened in August 1996, Full House said.
In addition, Full House said it cut non-resort general and administrative costs by 16.6 percent.

"Last year, we were able to successfully execute on opportunities, cut costs and focus on building and strengthening relationships that will position the Company for future growth," Full House chairman and chief executive Allen Paulson said in a statement. "We look forward to continuing our momentum throughout 1997."
Full House Resorts is a developer of entertainment, gaming and commercial centers.
Dreamport is the gaming and entertainment unit of GTECH Holdings Corp.
